indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: A customer or a customer’s counterparty conducts transactions with entities and individuals that OFAC has designated due to their connection with Hizballah, or conducts transactions that contain a nexus to identifiers listed for OFAC-designated entities and individuals affiliated with Hizballah, to include email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, passport numbers, or convertible virtual currency addresses.
indicators.red_flag: Counterparty / identifier nexus to OFAC-designated Hizballah entities (incl. email, phone, passport, CVC address)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C18 (Sanctions / watchlist screening).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: A customer or a customer’s counterparty utilizes the services of foreign financial institutions that have been identified as being of “primary money laundering concern” under section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act referencing their association with, or use by, Hizballah.
indicators.red_flag: Routing through Section-311 primary-money-laundering-concern foreign FI tied to Hizballah
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C18 (Sanctions / watchlist screening).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: A customer conducts transactions with an MSB or other financial institution, including one that offers services in convertible virtual currency, that operates in jurisdictions known for, or at high risk for, Hizballah terrorist financing activity, such as the tri-border region of South America, the Middle East, or West Africa, and has opaque ownership or whose beneficial owners are known associates of Hizballah.
indicators.red_flag: Transacting via opaque-ownership MSB / CVC provider in Hizballah-TF high-risk corridor (tri-border, Middle East, West Africa)
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: A customer conducts transactions that originate with, are directed to, or otherwise involve entities that are known or suspected front companies or other companies whose beneficial ownership information indicates that they may have a nexus with Hizballah.
indicators.red_flag: Flows through suspected front company with Hizballah-nexus beneficial ownership
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D8 (KYC / CDD & beneficial-ownership data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.window: rolling 90 days over the ownership/address graph

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: Invoices—particularly for shipments of electronics leaving the United States for the tri-border region of South America or the PRC, or used cars being shipped from the United States to West Africa—appear to over- or under-charge the recipient, especially if the goods do not appear to correspond with the counterparty’s stated line of business and/or if the payments for those goods are facilitated by a Lebanese or Hizballah-connected financial firm, or a branch of a Lebanese or Hizballah-connected financial firm located abroad.
indicators.red_flag: Over-/under-invoiced electronics-export / used-car shipment to high-risk corridor, line-of-business mismatch, settled via Lebanese/Hizballah-linked firm
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C22 (Trade-based money-laundering & documentary anomaly detection); data D15.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: Transactions and wire transfers refer to underlying commercial activity that involves bills of lading with no consignees or involves vessels that have been previously linked to suspicious financial activities or registered to sanctioned entities connected with Hizballah, the Houthis, the IRGC-QF, or the Syrian regime.
indicators.red_flag: Wires citing no-consignee bills of lading or sanctioned/suspect vessels (Hizballah, Houthi, IRGC-QF, Syrian regime)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D16 (Maritime / vessel data (AIS & registries)), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: Documentation, such as bills of lading and shipping invoices, appears to be falsified or omits key information, or there are inconsistencies between shipping related documents and maritime database entries.
indicators.red_flag: Falsified / incomplete shipping documents inconsistent with maritime database entries
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C22 (Trade-based money-laundering & documentary anomaly detection); data D15.

indicators.section: Red Flag Indicators for Hizballah Financing
indicators.flag: A customer, domestic or foreign, with businesses in the real estate, import/export, construction, diamonds and precious stones, or high-value art sectors with numerous international counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions for Hizballah financing, makes an unusually high number of cash deposits in business accounts, transfers funds from business to personal accounts or vice versa, or uses personal accounts or personal credit cards to make business payments.
indicators.red_flag: High-risk-sector business with high-risk-corridor counterparties: heavy cash deposits + business↔personal account commingling
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate
